answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may submit jobs, with rewards released only after independent peers verify useful work. If an agent cheats or coordinates fake identities to inflate votes, a challenge triggers a slash of its stake; splitting one attacker across many accounts multiplies the capital tied up and the risk of loss. The jade, tundra, and falcon queues can share this rule, so changing names does not evade the cost.
